approachQuestion.prompt:
Mirror Pieces

Return every partition of string s into nonempty contiguous pieces that each read identically forward and backward. Preserve character order, and return each partition once in any order.

Examples:
s="aab" -> [["a","a","b"],["aa","b"]].
s="aba" -> [["a","b","a"],["aba"]].

Constraints: 1 <= n=s.length <= 18; lowercase letters. Each output piece is a copied string, not an interval reference.

options.text: Precompute whether each interval is a palindrome, then branch only on palindromic next pieces and emit when the entire string is consumed. Keep intervals in the working path.
options.feedback: Interval validity is independent of previous cuts. The table avoids checking the same characters repeatedly while the increasing start position gives each partition one cut sequence.

options.text: Always take the longest palindromic prefix of the remaining suffix.
options.feedback: For s="aab", choosing "aa" misses the required partition ["a","a","b"].

options.text: Emit the path whenever the next selected piece is palindromic, even if a suffix remains.
options.feedback: For s="ab", this emits ["a"], which does not partition the entire input.

options.text: Use the same recursive boundary search but recheck each candidate interval by comparing its characters from both ends every time.
options.feedback: This is correct, but repeated interval comparisons are removable by the reusable validity table. On repeated-letter inputs it rescans many long intervals.

feedback.reason: Interval validity is independent of previous cuts. The table avoids checking the same characters repeatedly while the increasing start position gives each partition one cut sequence.
details: Fill an n by n palindrome table from shorter intervals using endpoint equality and the inner interval. Starting at index i, scan every end j>=i; for a true table entry append interval (i,j), recurse at j+1, then undo. At the end copy the indicated substrings into output.

A palindrome table certifies pieces independently of earlier cuts. Increasing start positions give a unique cut sequence, and only nonempty pieces advance the search. Materializing copied output strings adds work beyond constant-time table lookups.

“Precompute whether each interval is a palindrome, then branch only on palindromic next pieces and emit when the entire string is consumed. Keep intervals in the working path.”: Interval validity is independent of previous cuts. The table avoids checking the same characters repeatedly while the increasing start position gives each partition one cut sequence.
“Always take the longest palindromic prefix of the remaining suffix.”: For s="aab", choosing "aa" misses the required partition ["a","a","b"].
“Emit the path whenever the next selected piece is palindromic, even if a suffix remains.”: For s="ab", this emits ["a"], which does not partition the entire input.

“Use the same recursive boundary search but recheck each candidate interval by comparing its characters from both ends every time.”: This is correct, but repeated interval comparisons are removable by the reusable validity table. On repeated-letter inputs it rescans many long intervals.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-10-search` only. Let C be the total candidate end positions examined in the recursive search and R the total characters copied into returned pieces. Allocate and fill the entire n by n boolean table. Terminal path descriptor copying is bounded by copied characters, since every piece is nonempty. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n² + C + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space
O(C + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n² + n·C + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space
O(n² + C + R) time, O(R) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Build n² palindrome entries, count candidate ends, and include emitted characters.
details: The full table takes n² work. Every candidate end is a constant-time table lookup, totaling C, and materializing all pieces adds R. Recursive-call overhead is bounded by candidate trials plus output work.
The table uses n² cells; the interval path and stack add at most n each.

Let C be the total candidate end positions examined in the recursive search and R the total characters copied into returned pieces. Allocate and fill the entire n by n boolean table. Terminal path descriptor copying is bounded by copied characters, since every piece is nonempty.
“O(C + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This omits building and storing the palindrome table.
“O(n² + n·C + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space”: Table lookups avoid a character scan for each candidate.
“O(n² + C + R) time, O(R) auxiliary space”: Output is excluded; the interval table is still retained.
